model_format: navigator.userAgent verbatim, which is what both Telegram web clients send
version_format: navigator.platform -- Win32, MacIntel, or uname sysname + machine on Linux
sources: https://github.com/morethanwords/tweb/blob/master/src/lib/appManagers/networkerFactory.ts -- Telegram Web K: deviceModel = USER_AGENT, systemVersion = navigator.platform
https://github.com/Ajaxy/telegram-tt/blob/master/src/api/gramjs/methods/client.ts -- Telegram Web A: the same two fields
https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/components/embedder_support/user_agent_utils.cc -- the Chromium UA template and the frozen platform tokens
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/web-platform/user-agent-guidance -- the Edg token and where it goes
https://product-details.mozilla.org/1.0/firefox_history_major_releases.json -- released Firefox majors and their dates
notes: model is the whole User-Agent string, not a device name: a browser has no model to report, so both web clients send navigator.userAgent as it stands. This is also why a web session draws a browser icon in every client -- Telegram Android matches 'chrome'/'firefox'/'edge' inside device_model and Telegram Desktop matches 'chrome'/'firefox'/'edg/', both before they look at the platform.

Every string is generated from the browsers' own frozen templates rather than collected, because there is nothing left to collect: Chromium pins its platform token and its minor version, Gecko pins the Windows OS version to 10.0, and only the major version still moves. The majors and their dates come from each vendor's own release feed.
Only the newest 4 majors per browser and system are kept. Browsers update themselves, so a session further behind than that is not a realistic thing to report.
Desktop only, on purpose. A phone browser is a real web session but a rare one, and it would need its own frozen tokens and its own navigator.platform values to be honest rather than guessed.

Safari is absent: WebKit freezes the UA prefix but the 'Version/x.y Safari/605.1.15' suffix is Safari's own application name and Apple publishes no machine-readable version feed, so the numbers would have to be invented. macOS is still covered, by Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
Each device lists exactly one version because a UA and navigator.platform describe the same machine: a UA claiming Windows cannot report 'MacIntel'.
